mike_h: Hey team — customer acme-inc (acct 74219) raised a billing delta on INV-2026-03. They see ~3.1k tokens in the usage dashboard for a batch of streamed chat requests but the invoice contains ~7.0k tokens. All traffic went to /v1/chat/stream (SSE). They say the client cancels mid-generation frequently. Can we triage?

priya_r: Thanks — can you drop a sample request_id and any server logs? Also any repro steps from the client would help. @taylor_eng @billing-bot

mike_h: request_id: r_0a9f3c72. Customer repro steps: 1) open SSE stream 2) client sends messages and cancels client-side after ~350 tokens 3) reconnects immediately to start a new message. They attached a short client trace. Server snippets: ```
[2026-03-12T18:21:34Z] r_0a9f3c72 stream-start session=ses-9c
[2026-03-12T18:21:35Z] r_0a9f3c72 chunk sent token_delta=328
[2026-03-12T18:21:36Z] r_0a9f3c72 client disconnect (code=1001)
[2026-03-12T18:21:36Z] r_0a9f3c72 final_event emitted id=evt-F1 tokens=32
[2026-03-12T18:21:36Z] r_0a9f3c72 ingest received final_event id=evt-F1 tokens=32
[2026-03-12T18:21:37Z] r_0a9f3c72 reconnect session=ses-9c new_request=r_0a9f3c73
[2026-03-12T18:21:37Z] r_0a9f3c73 start resumed previous_partial_id=evt-F1
```

taylor_eng: Looks like the pipeline is ingesting the final_event twice when a reconnect references previous_partial_id. We recently changed semantics around resume support to accept previous_partial_id for continuity; it seems we didn't dedupe final_event ids in the streaming ingestion path. That would create duplicated token counts (final fragment counted at original close AND again when resumed).

billing-bot: Reconciler job finished 03/12/2026 18:30Z. Preliminary credit calc: potential double-count between dashboard and invoice = 3,880 tokens for acct 74219.

priya_r: Can eng run an aggregation query to confirm which final_event ids are duplicated across request_ids for that session window? If confirmed, we'll apply a one-time credit and patch ingestion.

ingest-bot: Query results: final_event ids for ses-9c showing duplicates: [evt-F1] appeared in r_0a9f3c72 and r_0a9f3c73. Total duplicated tokens = 3,904.

mike_h: Confirmed with customer that their client reconnects within 1s after cancel. They can reproduce reliably.

taylor_eng: Root cause summary: resume flow accepted previous_partial_id and re-emitted the last partial as part of the resumed session; ingestion didn't have idempotency for final_event emissions. Fix: (1) dedupe by final_event id at ingest (2) ignore re-emit if final_event timestamp < 10s and request_id differs but session id matches. I'll prepare a small hotfix on the stream-ingest lambda, then roll to prod.

priya_r: Billing action: we'll apply a credit of 3,904 tokens (~$0.78) to INV-2026-03 and add a note. Customer will be notified.

mike_h: Patch deployed to canary at 18:45Z and then prod at 19:02Z. Observability: no more duplicate final_event hits in the sample window.

customer_ops: Customer ACKed credit and patch, asked for a short doc on client-side best practice (delay 2s before immediate reconnect). Can we provide one?

taylor_eng: I'll open a quick KB and add suggestion: when client cancels, include a short randomized backoff before reconnect OR attach a new session id instead of resuming partials unless you want strictly continuous generations.

priya_r: Closing loop: credit applied, ingest dedupe in prod, KB in progress. Marking thread resolved for billing reconciliation. :white_check_mark:
